title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 338 (Liability where proper accounts not kept)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up, if it is shown that proper books of account were not kept by the company throughout the period of two years immediately preceding the commencement of the winding up, or the period between incorporation and commencement (whichever is shorter), every officer of the company who is in default shall, unless he shows that he acted honestly and that in the circumstances the default was excusable, be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one year but which may extend to three years and with fine which shall not be less than one lakh rupees but which may extend to three lakh rupees.
content.glance: Failure to keep proper books for the two years (or shorter incorporation period) before winding up attracts 1–3 years’ imprisonment and fine for officers in default, subject to honest-and-excusable defence.
content.study: Section 338 imposes criminal liability for failure to keep proper books of account in the period immediately before winding up. The relevant period is two years before commencement, or from incorporation if shorter. Every officer in default is punishable unless he shows he acted honestly and the default was excusable in the circumstances. Penalty is imprisonment of not less than one year and up to three years, and fine of not less than one lakh and up to three lakh rupees.

sections.heading: Duty period
sections.body: Two years immediately preceding commencement of winding up, or from incorporation if shorter.

sections.heading: Liability and defence
sections.body: Officer in default punishable unless he proves he acted honestly and the default was excusable.

provisions.title: Liability where proper accounts not kept

examples.title: Missing books
examples.body: In a Tribunal winding up it is shown that no proper books were kept for the eighteen months before the order. An officer in default is liable under s. 338 unless he establishes the honest-and-excusable defence.

hypotheticals.question: Is the absence of books for only one year before winding up enough for liability?
hypotheticals.analysis: The statutory period is two years (or from incorporation if shorter). Liability turns on failure throughout that period; shorter gaps may still be relevant on the facts.

rows.left: Liability where proper accounts not kept

misconceptions.correction: The officer can avoid liability by showing he acted honestly and the default was excusable in the circumstances.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 338. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.
